rows: What defines a vertebrate?
Notochord, dorsal nerve cord, pharyngeal slits at some stage — vertebrates add vertebral column, neural crest cells
What were the first jawed fish?
Acanthodians (Silurian); placoderms dominated Devonian; both predate sharks and bony fish
What is Tiktaalik?
375 Ma sarcopterygian "fishapod" — fish with neck, ribs, and wrist joint; predicted from phylogenetic gap, found on Ellesmere Island
Why did tetrapod limbs evolve in water first?
Acanthostega (365 Ma) had 8-toed limbs but preserved internal gills → limbs adapted for aquatic maneuvering, not land walking
What is the amniotic egg?
A cleidoic egg with amnion/chorion/allantois/yolk sac membranes enabling fully terrestrial reproduction; evolved ~315 Ma
What makes synapsids special?
They're on the mammal lineage: single temporal fenestra; jaw bones progressively reduced → middle ear ossicles → better hearing
What is Morganucodon?
~200 Ma transitional form with BOTH reptilian and mammalian jaw joints simultaneously — a classic transitional fossil
What is the order of feather evolution?
Protofilaments → tuft → rachis → pennaceous → asymmetric; insulation/display first; flight capability much later
Are birds dinosaurs?
Yes — Aves is a subgroup of Maniraptora within Theropoda within Dinosauria. Velociraptor is more closely related to birds than to T. rex
What is Archaeopteryx?
~150 Ma early avialian from Solnhofen with mosaic of dinosaurian and avian features; one of the best transitional fossils known
